title: 2001 HMMT February Guts Problem 7
statement: Suppose \(a, b, c, d\), and \(e\) are objects that we can multiply together, but the multiplication doesn't necessarily satisfy the associative law, i.e. ( \(x y\) ) z does not necessarily equal \(x(y z)\). How many different ways are there to interpret the product \(a b c d e\) ?
